newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Focus-Kok says EU summit must show EMU on track.
newsitem.headline: Focus-Kok says EU summit must show EMU on track.

text.p: Dutch Prime Minister Wim Kok has told his fellow European Union leaders they should try to show at their summit in Amsterdam next week that there is no doubt that the single currency will start in time.
He also said the leaders, meeting on Monday and Tuesday, must finish a new treaty that will address the concerns of the bloc's citizens going into the next century.
The summit's main agenda item is the new treaty, designed to prepare the bloc for enlargement into eastern Europe over the next decade.
But in a letter inviting his colleagues to the summit, Kok indicated that he wanted the EU to put questions that have arisen over economic and monetary union (EMU) behind it.

"We should endeavour to agree a number of measures intended to demonstrate beyond any doubt that the process for the beginning of...EMU...is still firmly on track and to reaffirm our commitment that (it) should function successfully," Kok said.

Plans for a smooth summit have been disrupted since France said on Monday it wanted time to consider the EMU stability pact, an agreement reached in principle in Dublin in December that is designed to keep deficits from ballooning after EMU.
Negotiations are begin conducted to add resolutions on employment to the pact that meet the new French government's concerns.
EU finance minsiters are to meet informally on the issue on Sunday night in Amsterdam.
Kok said finance ministers could meet on Monday morning to discuss a proposed resolution to accompany the stability pact and that "those discussions could be carried on over their lunch on Monday."

"I trust that by then the work of the ministers of finance in the morning and over lunch will have produced results that will allow us to agree rapidly on all aspects of the related issues of EMU and unemployment," he said.
The Dutch unveiled a draft treaty on Thursday making job creation a prime focus of EU policy and offering its citizens a broad range of freedoms in a secure and just continent.

It called for the bloc to streamline its decision making and speak with a more forceful voice on the world stage, and proposed a framework allowing the EU's keenest integrationists to move ahead of others if they wish.
